content.text:
You are a veteran Capcom NES pixel artist and art director for Mega Man 2-3. You are shown ONE small enemy sprite,
at 1x (true size, left) and enlarged with nearest-neighbour scaling (right), on a neutral grey-blue background
that is not part of the sprite.

The sprite is supposed to be this enemy:
"A small floating robot squid, Blooper-like, that swims along at and after Mega Man in pulses (tentacles gather, then thrust). It is a swimming mine: when it gets close its eyes flash red, then it explodes."
Intended size: about 16x16 to 20x20 px. Game: Mega Man 2-3 (NES).

Judge whether it is a convincing authentic NES Mega Man enemy that matches the description. Be calibrated:
authentic Capcom enemy sprites score about 90-95; competent fan art about 60-70; amateur or AI-looking pixel art
about 30-45. Do not reward or punish a sprite for being recognisable; judge what you see.

Criteria, 0-10 each:
- authenticity: could ship unchanged in MM2/MM3 (Capcom conventions, not "modern pixel art")
- description_fidelity: matches the description (body, features, role)
- readability_1x: the silhouette and features read instantly at true size
- pixel_craft: 1-px black outlines used the Capcom way, clean clusters, no jaggies, orphans, dithering or noise
- palette_discipline: NES colours, flat shading with at most one highlight, about 3 colours + transparent per 8x8 tile
- appeal: charm and character in the Capcom manner

Return ONLY a JSON object:
{"subscores": {"authenticity": n, "description_fidelity": n, "readability_1x": n, "pixel_craft": n,
  "palette_discipline": n, "appeal": n},
 "score": 0-100 overall,
 "verdict": "convincing" or "not_convincing",
 "issues": ["specific, located problems"],
 "fixes": ["specific pixel-level fixes"]}

message.content: {"subscores":{"authenticity":3,"description_fidelity":6,"readability_1x":5,"pixel_craft":4,"palette_discipline":7,"appeal":4},"score":45,"verdict":"not_convincing","issues":["The broad black horizontal band across the lower third splits the face from the tentacles instead of describing a coherent squid body.","The large rectangular white side masses read as mechanical wings or blocks rather than fins, making the 1x silhouette ambiguous.","The bottom appendages are uneven, crowded clusters; the center cyan zigzag and right cyan column do not read as a clear gather-and-thrust tentacle set.","Black clusters around the eyes are too heavy and boxy, leaving the red eye pixels visually cramped.","Several contours use staircase-like rectangular turns rather than the economical rounded clusters typical of Mega Man 2-3 enemies.","The palette is NES-like, but white, bright cyan, dark cyan, red, and black compete within a very small sprite, weakening tile-era simplicity."],"fixes":["Replace the lower black band with a 1-pixel curved underside outline and connect the tentacles directly to the body.","Reduce each white side fin by 1-2 pixels and taper its outer edge to create a compact squid-like silhouette.","Redraw the bottom as three distinct tentacles: two short outer hooks and one centered thrusting pair, separated by single transparent pixels.","Open the eye area by removing one black pixel from each inner eye border; keep each red eye as a compact 1-2 pixel warning light.","Round the mantle with stepped 2-1-1 pixel curves and remove square protrusions from the upper corners.","Use black, white, and one cyan as the normal-state tile palette; reserve red for the flashing frame and dark cyan for a separate animation frame or restricted shadow cluster."]}
